reading: TileWeb brings together a divided archive of roughly 3,000 watercolours of historic paving tiles, connecting collections in Worcester and Oxford. It treats tiles as evidence of the tastes of craftspeople and patrons, tracing designs, materials, manufacture, locations and the movement of ideas across centuries and cultures. Its language is that of architectural ceramics, pavements, motifs, heraldry, watercolours, surveys, in situ finds and catalogues. The archive is also a family story of a granddaughter completing a long-running undertaking, and a community project assembled through museum collaboration, volunteers and scanning. Its distinctive setting ranges from county-coded records to a hidden Oxford library with a surveyed tiled floor; the site cares as much about reuniting scattered evidence and recording where tiles belonged as about preserving their patterns.

enemies.idea: Reunion Engine: a many-jointed collector that drags distant tile fragments together, forcing unrelated pieces into a single pavement and pinning anything caught between them.
enemies.why: Its desire to complete a divided archive creates moving terrain and a puzzle about separating pieces without breaking them.

enemies.idea: Patron's Appraiser: a ceramic hound that sniffs out a person's tastes and stamps them onto tiles, then hunts anyone whose choices fail its ever-changing standard of refinement.
enemies.why: It turns the archive's reading of patrons' tastes into a fickle social predator.

enemies.idea: A3 Sweepers: flat, wide machines that pass over watercolours and living intruders alike, pressing everything into flawless, immobile copies.
enemies.why: Their slow scanning passes create clear safe zones, while the copies can be mistaken for the originals.

enemies.idea: Benefit Auditor: a tiled clerk that measures every act against its own idea of community benefit and confiscates anything it cannot quantify.
enemies.why: A well-meant evaluation becomes a negotiation with absurd but consistent rules.

enemies.idea: Court Metalworker: a jointed smith that embosses the floor with molten-looking metal patterns which cool into clamps around passing feet.
enemies.why: The proposed metalworking origins of pavement design become a readable attack with a brief escape window.

enemies.idea: Cosmati Millipede: a mosaic creature whose porphyry, marble and glass segments detach into a glittering maze, then reassemble behind its prey.
enemies.why: Mixed stone and glass make each segment behave differently as cover, mirror or obstacle.

enemies.idea: Provenance Retriever: a machine that insists every tile return to its recorded location, including tiles now stored safely in a museum; it takes the floor out from under the crew to enforce its map.
enemies.why: The conflict between original context and safe storage turns the battlefield into a shifting argument.

enemies.idea: Silk-Roundel Weaver: a loom-legged hunter that casts pearl-ringed nets and repeats captured silhouettes as decorative motifs.
enemies.why: Textile patterns cross into tilework as traps that multiply the crew's own outlines.

enemies.idea: Innovation Carrier: a little courier that steals one tactic from anyone it meets and spreads it to nearby swarm machines, unless interrupted before its next delivery.
enemies.why: The spread of technological and artistic ideas becomes an escalating tactical problem.

enemies.idea: Heraldic Misidentifier: an armoured classifier that assigns combatants imaginary coats of arms, then redirects other machines toward anyone carrying a matching pattern.
enemies.why: Identification in armour becomes a game of swapping or obscuring marks to confuse the swarm.

enemies.idea: Alphabet Press: a square-jawed tile creature that captures letters from spoken words and lays them as a wall; a missing letter leaves a gap to squeeze through.
enemies.why: Initial and alphabet tiles make speech itself a resource and a hazard.

enemies.idea: Garment Mimic: a figurative tile figure that borrows the detailed clothing of whoever it sees and lures machines toward its chosen double.
enemies.why: The archive's carefully observed garments support a playful disguise and mistaken-identity encounter.

enemies.idea: Geometer: a mechanical draughtsman that extends repeating geometric designs across floors and walls, dividing rooms into ever-smaller compartments.
enemies.why: A repeating design becomes a spatial puzzle whose rhythm can be disrupted.

enemies.idea: Knot-Garden Strangler: a swarm of ceramic knot motifs that loops around obstacles and tightens whenever the crew pulls directly against it.
enemies.why: The knot's logic rewards slackening and rerouting over brute force.

enemies.idea: Northkeeper: a survey instrument on tile legs that rotates whole floor sections to keep its internal north at the top, regardless of where people stand.
enemies.why: The survey's orientation becomes a navigational hazard with a predictable rule.

enemies.idea: Discipline Sorter: a library automaton that files people under theology, classics, science, medicine or mathematics and seals them into separate patterned chambers.
enemies.why: Its categories invite the crew to argue for unexpected connections between subjects to reunite.

enemies.idea: Bibliographic Cross-Referencer: a chain of ceramic volumes that cites other volumes as reinforcements; breaking a citation loop makes the chain lose its place.
enemies.why: A scholarly bibliography becomes a fight about tracing and interrupting dependencies.

enemies.idea: County Boundary Patrol: numbered tile machines that keep shifting the border between Hampshire and Bedfordshire and demand that travelers be catalogued on the correct side.
enemies.why: County and catalogue labels provide a concrete bureaucratic obstacle whose border can be negotiated or outwitted.

allies.idea: The Watercolour Keeper preserves translucent impressions of missing tiles and can show a crew how a pavement looked before the swarm rearranged it.
allies.why: A family archive's long continuity supplies a humane guide and useful visual clues.

allies.idea: Volunteer Scanners carry portable light frames that reveal the original drawing beneath a machine's ceramic disguise, though they need someone to hold the subject still.
allies.why: The people who assembled the archive become practical collaborators in exposing the swarm.

allies.idea: The In-Situ Surveyor marks where displaced tiles were found and can temporarily persuade a retrieval machine to release one by showing it a conflicting record.
allies.why: Careful provenance creates a nonviolent way to challenge the machines' certainty.

allies.idea: The Hidden Librarian shelters travelers in a little room above the tiled pavement and lends them subject knowledge to solve the floor's changing patterns.
allies.why: The barely known library becomes a refuge with a direct relationship to the danger below.

bosses.idea: The Grand Reunifier wears thousands of mismatched watercolour tiles as a body and tries to make one perfect pavement from every separated collection, including the crew's equipment. Its joints open when contradictory provenances are placed side by side.
bosses.why: The entire project's ambition to reunite a divided archive becomes an enormous, understandable threat with a research-based weakness.

bosses.idea: The Master Pavement is a mobile floor that combines court metalwork, mosaic, heraldry, letters and knots into successive defenses. It keeps rewriting its own design as it absorbs ideas from across the archive.
bosses.why: The whole study of architectural ceramics becomes a staged encounter in which earlier pattern knowledge pays off.

bosses.idea: The Library Underfoot is a walking tiled pavement carrying a miniature library on its back; it sorts every captured object by subject while rotating its floor to enforce its own survey orientation.
bosses.why: The site's hidden library and surveyed pavement become one moving place to explore and escape.

events.idea: Two separated watercolor fragments each show half a design. A reunion machine is approaching; matching them may reveal a safe route before it forcibly joins everything nearby.
events.why: A small act of archival reconstruction doubles as a time-sensitive route puzzle.

events.idea: A scanner is making duplicate impressions of a volunteer's notes, but each pass erases one colour from the original. The crew can redirect the light or reconstruct the missing hues.
events.why: Digitisation becomes a delicate rescue with useful evidence at stake.

events.idea: A tile insists it belongs in a church floor while its museum storage crate insists it is safer inside. Both have plausible records, and a retriever is closing in.
events.why: Preservation and original context produce a choice without an automatic right answer.

events.idea: A procession of armoured machines halts at a heraldic crossroads, unable to tell friend from foe after their patterns have been swapped. A crew can rearrange the marks to pass.
events.why: Heraldry's identifying function becomes a compact social and visual puzzle.

events.idea: Alphabet tiles are spelling a warning one letter at a time, but a hungry press is stealing the vowels. Recovering a few letters reveals where the floor is unsafe.
events.why: Reading the room becomes literal and rewards intervention before the message disappears.

events.idea: A pearl-roundel net is snagged on a floor mosaic. Loosening its repeated loops frees a trapped surveyor but risks letting the weaving machine sense the movement.
events.why: A textile-derived motif offers a tactile rescue puzzle.

events.idea: A courier is teaching nearby machines a new way around a barricade. The crew can intercept its route, send it in circles or feed it a harmless technique.
events.why: Ideas spreading at different speeds become a problem with several possible solutions.

events.idea: In the hidden library, books on mathematics and medicine have been sorted into separate locked alcoves, but a shared clue is needed to open both.
events.why: The breadth of the collection encourages cooperation across artificial categories.

events.idea: A north-pointing survey marker keeps swiveling as the pavement turns. Aligning it with the room rather than the moving tiles reveals a concealed path.
events.why: Orientation is a physical puzzle grounded in the floor survey.

events.idea: A glass mosaic segment reflects a doorway that the surrounding stone segments conceal. The crew must choose which pieces to move without scattering the whole floor.
events.why: The different materials of a Cosmati pavement give exploration a concrete visual trick.

events.idea: A county-labelled tile patrol has seized a box whose catalogue number belongs to a neighboring county. The crew can trace the record or invent a convincing transfer.
events.why: County and record identifiers generate a small bureaucratic standoff.

events.idea: A trail of painted garment details leads to a figurative tile whose missing companion is being used as a machine's disguise. Reuniting the pair earns a clue to the next room.
events.why: Close observation of the drawings turns into a distinctive search.

events.idea: A pavement of rosettes and knots tightens around a dropped tool. The pattern loosens if its loops are followed backward, but pulling the tool makes it cinch.
events.why: A familiar decorative knot becomes an intuitive hands-on problem.

events.idea: An appraiser offers safe passage if the crew can explain what a damaged tile reveals about its maker or patron; several different observations can satisfy it.
events.why: The archive's interpretive question becomes an invitation to notice details rather than a test of trivia.
